comment: Every place this package's ESLint config deliberately differs from obsidian-dev-utils' shared config, and why.
This package is that package's sibling and resolves no dependency on it, so `scripts/eslint-config.ts` is a HAND
COPY - and a hand copy drifts silently, which it did for eighteen months. update-npm-deps.ps1 compares the two
configs on every dependency sweep and fails on anything not recorded here.
The comparison is DIRECTIONAL: only 'obsidian-dev-utils refined something and this copy never took it' is a
finding. A rule this package enables that obsidian-dev-utils turns off is printed as information and never fails,
because this copy is then the stricter one and obsidian-dev-utils' reasons for its own relaxations are
A key is the finding's identity exactly as the check prints it: <role>|<rule>|<kind>[|<detail>]. The
correspondence runs BOTH ways - an entry describing a divergence that no longer exists fails the sweep too, which
is what stops this file going stale the way the comments at the call sites did. Add `task` when the entry is an
adoption intended for later rather than a settled decision; it is then re-reported on every run.
`roles` names the file compared at each end. Only the `script` role is compared by default, because it is the one
role that plays the same part in both packages.
The `workflow-scripts/` subpackage is a SECOND hand copy with its own package.json, node_modules and eslint
config, and it carries its own copy of this file. Sweeping this package does not sweep that one.

script|no-console|level.why: The build, lint, format, docs and version scripts are CLI entry points whose output IS their interface, so printing to stdout is what they are for. obsidian-dev-utils leaves the rule on everywhere because nothing in that package prints.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/no-over-cap-wa.why: This package vendors a five-rule subset of obsidian-dev-utils' custom rules into `scripts/helpers/eslint-rules/`; its plugin file's `rules` map IS that subset. This rule polices an integration suite's `evalInObsidian` wait budget, and this package has no such suite.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/prefer-noop-as.why: Not vendored - same subset reason. Only `obsidian-test-mocks` vendors this sixth rule, which its own consumer table records.

script|obsidian-dev-utils/require-compon.why: Not vendored - same subset reason. Obsidian `Component` subclasses are a plugin-authoring shape; this package ships type declarations.

script|unicorn/name-replacements|option|.why: Only the `direction` expansion of `dir` is dropped here - every `dir` in this repo is a filesystem directory - so `dir` still expands to `directory` by the rule's own default rather than by an entry saying so.

Not in this repo's vocabulary list, so `dist` is expanded here rather than allowed. The list is the established vocabulary of THIS repo (`doc`/`docs`, `param`/`params`, `prop`/`props`, `src`, `attr`, `desc`, `dev`, `ref`), not a copy of obsidian-dev-utils'.
Not in this repo's vocabulary list - same reason as `dist`.
Not in this repo's vocabulary list - same reason as `dist`.

script|unicorn/no-top-level-assignment-i.why: Measured with the rule on: four sites, three of them test fixtures assigned from `beforeEach` in `scripts/helpers/package-manager.test.ts` - the shape obsidian-dev-utils exempts over its own test files - and the fourth a module-level memo in `docs/scripts/helpers/api-doc-link-rendering.ts`. Off repo-wide rather than only over test files, because the memo is production code here.

script|unicorn/prefer-type-literal-last|.why: Unsatisfiable alongside `perfectionist/sort-union-types`, which this config takes from `recommended-alphabetical`. Measured rather than assumed: with this rule on and unfixed, perfectionist reports 0 and this rule 66; after its autofix the two counts swap exactly. Both are `error` and neither concedes. The alphabetical sort is the incumbent.
